newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebel again warns Arakis Corp on oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebel again warns Arakis Corp on oil deal.

text.p: Sudanese rebel leader John Garang on Monday repeated his warning to Canada's Arakis Energy Corp that his forces would strike if needed to halt any attempts to develop its concessions in southern Sudan.

Asked about unconfirmed reports that his troops had fired at Arakis oil fields in war-ravaged southern Sudan, Garang told a news conference he was not aware of the reports but asked Arakis to leave the area.

"What are they doing in southern Sudan? We have warned them that this is a no-go area. It is a legitimate military target," Garang, head of the rebel South Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), told the news conference.
He added: "I do not know if they (SPLA troops) fired at Arakis oil fields, but if they did I say congratulations."

In October, Garang had warned Arakis not to go ahead with an oil deal that would benefit Khartoum after the Canadian firm announced it was close to signing a deal with other firms to develop its Heglig and Unity fields in Sudan and build a 500-mile (800 km) pipeline to the Red Sea from the fields.
The Sudanese government will refine the oil.
Garang's SPLA is the largest and oldest southern Sudanese rebel group fighting for greater independence for the mainly Christian and animist south of Sudan from the Molsem, Arabised north.
The SPLA has been fighting since 1983.
Garang said a newly formed committee by the Eritrean-based opposition to coordinate military operations against the Islamist government held its first meeting last Thursday and Friday.
The committee formed in October and headed by Garang includes the SPLA and the opposition National Democratic Alliance (NDA) forces and the little-known Beja Congress.
The rebel leader said the rebel alliance had intensified its military campaign against government forces in one of Africa's longest-running civil wars.

"The committee held its first meeting in the Kassala area last week from December 5 to 6. This plus the intensification of operations in the eastern front provoked the government to declare a state of emergency in Kassala state," Garang added.

Garang said the committee adopted resolutions on the "concept and mode of military operations, training, mobilisation of resources for execution of the war and intensification of military operations".

Garang said the rebel alliance had been fighting government forces in eastern Sudan for the last four days and casualties from the fighting included a Lieutenant-Colonel Mohamed Khalifa, a member of Khartoum's powerful National Islamic Front (NIF).
The war has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced and sent into exile many more.
Eritrea, which says Sudan's Islamic government of General Omar Hassan al-Bashir is trying to destabilise the region, supports the Sudanese rebels in their campaign against the government.
